title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A 'disposition' on a set E is a symmetric relation x|0|y, here a disjointness or orthogonality relation; the transcription writes it |0| and |∘| interchangeably. For a subset B ⊂ E:
- cosupp°_E(B) = {x ∈ E | x|0|B}, the orthogonal B^⊥.
- supp°_E(A) = cosupp°(cosupp°(A)) = A^⊥⊥, a closure operator.
- Σ_E is the set of closed subsets (A = A^⊥⊥). It is a complete ortholattice with orthocomplement C B = B^⊥; S denotes this complementation structure.

A correspondence α from E to E' has an image map ᾱ on subsets. The induced map is α_*: Σ_E → Σ_E', α_*(A) = supp°_E'(ᾱ(A)), the closure of the image. 'α compatible with the dispositions' means x|0|y ⇒ ᾱ(x)|0|ᾱ(y).

What the page does.
1. It finishes the reduction begun on p.59. Assume the 'dual' formula (**) α_*(cosupp°_E B) = cosupp°_E'(ᾱ(B)) for all B. Applying it twice gives α_*(supp°_E A) = cosupp°_E'(cosupp°_E'(ᾱ(A))) = supp°_E'(ᾱ(A)), which is formula (*).
2. For B ∈ Σ_E, (**) reads α_*(B^⊥) = ᾱ(B)^⊥ = (ᾱ(B)^⊥⊥)^⊥ = (α_*B)^⊥. In other words, the boxed identity α_*(CB) = Cα_*(B): α_* preserves orthocomplementation. Grothendieck therefore calls (**) 'la formule-clef'.
3. He starts proving (**). Write C = B^⊥, so (**) becomes (ᾱ(C))^⊥⊥ = ᾱ(B)^⊥.
   - The inclusion ⊂ reduces to ᾱ(C) ⊂ ᾱ(B)^⊥, i.e. ᾱ(C) |0| ᾱ(B).
   - This follows (finished on p.61) from B|0|C and compatibility, since the right-hand side is already closed.
4. The next page treats the reverse inclusion. It notes this cannot follow from compatibility alone and gives the counterexample of the tautological disposition x|0|y ⇔ x ≠ y:
   - Then Σ = 𝔓(E), and compatibility means α is injective.
   - α_*(A) = α(A) does not commute with complements unless α is surjective.

Purpose: to decide when a disposition-preserving correspondence induces a morphism of the associated ortholattices of closed sets. The answer is: not in general.
errors: The key formula (**), and hence α_*(CB) = Cα_*(B), is false under mere compatibility of α with the dispositions. Grothendieck himself discovers this on the next page (injective non-surjective map with the disposition x≠y). So the 'qed' at the top of this page is conditional on an unproved, generally false formula.
On p.59 he had already suspected the direct proof of (*) fails ('ça doit être faux'). Only the inclusion ⊂ of (**) holds in general.

ideas.what: Disposition = symmetric (irreflexive) orthogonality relation; closure A ↦ A^⊥⊥; lattice Σ_E of closed sets with orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space (Dacey space) and its complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets; Galois connection

ideas.what: Induced map α_* = closure of image for an orthogonality-preserving correspondence; question whether it preserves orthocomplement; reduction to α_*(B^⊥) = ᾱ(B)^⊥
ideas.modern_name: morphisms of orthogonality spaces vs. ortholattice homomorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; recent study by Paseka–Vetterlein and others

ideas.what: Easy inclusion ᾱ(B^⊥) ⊂ ᾱ(B)^⊥ from preservation of orthogonality

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, standard material on orthogonality spaces and biorthogonal closure. The attempted key formula is false, as Grothendieck himself notes on the next page. Nothing new for specialists beyond the biographical interest of seeing him work on such structures in 1986.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'dans supp°_E(A)' should read 'α_* supp°_E(A)' (the scribble is α_*).
The marginal parenthesis reads '(C = cosupp°_E(B))', with index E, not E'.
The last struck fragment is 'B|0|' (the image shows 'B|0' crossed out), continuing on the next page as 'B |0|_E C'.
